stories.title: Update: Jamia campus gates stay shut as four students continue hunger strike, with heavy security outside
stories.body:
Jamia Millia Islamia's main entry gates, libraries and canteens remained closed on Sunday 25 October, with all classes online until further notice, according to a registrar's notice cited by The Daily Jagran. The Federal, Siasat Daily and The Hans India reported that four students were still on hunger strike on Sunday, in a protest that began on Monday 12 October over the students' union election schedule, disciplinary action and the Chief Proctor. They said large numbers of security personnel were deployed, access through Gate No. 7 and nearby gates was restricted, and police used loudspeakers asking protesters to leave the campus and adjoining footpaths. Students alleged they were barred from bringing in food and water; no official response to this was quoted.

The Federal reported about 200 students inside the campus.
stories.check: NEEDS CHECK: The Daily Jagran says police detained four people, including three female student leaders, but does not attribute the figure to police; The Federal reports no detentions; Siasat says detentions were not confirmed and cites a student group's claim. Confirm with Delhi Police and Jamia. Food and water allegations are students' claims. Day count of the strike varies (the agitation began 12 Oct).

stories.title: Update: Jamia staff condemn wall slogans, march to protest site; university moves classes online
stories.body: A Jamia Millia Islamia press release issued by the Chief Public Relations Officer on Saturday 24 October says more than 1,500 teaching and non-teaching staff met that morning at the Ansari Auditorium lawns and passed two resolutions: urging protesters to leave the Ghalib statue lawns, and repainting or covering defaced walls. The release condemns what it calls highly objectionable slogans on campus walls and says staff later marched to the protest site at Gate No. 7, where, it says, guards, staff and teachers were pushed; staff withdrew and the administration moved all courses online. It says gates and libraries will stay closed until further notice. A separate release the same day carries an appeal to protesting students from the university's High Level Committee.
stories.check: NEEDS CHECK: The account of the confrontation is the university's; students' version was not found in the release. The text of the High Level Committee appeal (release 6174) could not be read because the PDF is garbled, so its contents are not reported here. The release pages carry no printed date; the 24 Oct date comes from the PDF text and file names.

CV Raman Marg Daily Brief, Mon 26 Oct

Jamia: gates and libraries stay closed and classes remain online; four students were still on hunger strike on Sun 25 Oct (The Federal, Siasat). Heavy security outside; reports differ on whether police detained anyone.

Jamia staff (1,500+, per the university's 24 Oct release) condemned wall slogans and called on protesters to leave the Ghalib lawns.

No confirmed BSES, DJB, MCD or Delhi Traffic Police items for our localities.
